sentences.text: Patagopelta was an extinct ankylosaurian dinosaur belonging to the class Ornithischia that lived in Argentina during the Late Cretaceous period.

This species is distinguished by high crests on the lateral elements of its neck osteoderms and a high crest on the anterior part of its femur, features reflected in the specific name cristata, which means crested in Latin.
A femur fossil of Patagopelta has been found with a length of only 25 centimeters.
Patagopelta possessed a distinctive frond-like tail weapon, similar to those seen in related parankylosaur genera.
New material suggests that Patagopelta was more heavily armored, robustly built, and larger than the related parankylosaurs Stegouros and Antarctopelta.
Fossils of Patagopelta were discovered in the Allen Formation at the Salitral Moreno locality near General Roca in the Río Negro Province of Argentina.
Initial remains were described in 1996 and were frequently referred to in literature as the Argentine ankylosaur.
Patagopelta cristata was formally described as a new genus and species in 2022 by a team of researchers including Facundo Riguetti and Victoria Arbour.

Patagopelta shared its habitat with birds like Lamarqueavis and Limenavis, pterosaurs like Aerotitan, rhynchosaurs like Lamarquesaurus, plesiosaurs like Kawanectes, and mammals like dryolesteoids and gondwanatherians.

Although originally classified within the family Nodosauridae, later evidence suggested Patagopelta belonged to the Parankylosauria, though Riguetti et al. 2022 recovered it as a member of Nodosaurinae contrasting with previous analyses that placed it in Panoplosaurini.
Patagopelta lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago, specifically from the upper Campanian to lower Maastrichtian ages.

It is debated whether Patagopelta is a nodosaurid or a parankylosaurian, with 2024 studies suggesting affinities with parankylosaurs like Antarctopelta, while Agnolín et al. 2026 reported new fossil material supporting the placement of Patagopelta within Parankylosauria.
